title: Time / JAMA: ICE Detention Fatality Rate Reaches 22-Year High; 35+ Dead Since October
excerpt: A Time investigation drawing on JAMA research found that the fatality rate in ICE custody had reached a 22-year high during the opening months of fiscal year 2026, with the rate nearly seven times the FY 2023 level. Over 35 people had died in ICE detention since October 2025.
content:
A Time magazine investigation published August 10, 2026, drawing on a peer-reviewed study published in the Journal of the American Medical Association (JAMA), reported that the fatality rate in ICE custody had reached a 22-year high.

The JAMA study found that the death rate for fiscal year 2026 was the highest in the 22-year study period, exceeding even the COVID-19 era spike. The rate reached 88.9 deaths per 100,000 person-years — nearly seven times the FY 2023 level of 13.0.

  • JAMA researchers described the spike as reflecting not isolated lapses but "systemic weaknesses in medical care, mental health protection, and mortality review" in a population wholly dependent on the state.
  • More than 35 people had died in ICE detention between October 2025 and the publication date; at least 17 additional deaths had occurred since the JAMA study's data cutoff of January 19, 2026.
  • By comparison, only 3 people died in ICE detention during the entire FY 2022 fiscal year.
  • The Time report documented individual cases of preventable deaths, including a Cambodian American father found unresponsive in Philadelphia whose family still lacked answers months later.

The investigation also noted that amid rising fatalities, ICE had reduced the information it makes public about detainee deaths — and had announced in June 2026 it would stop reporting deaths that occur shortly after release from custody altogether.
source: Time / Journal of the American Medical Association (JAMA)
